title: Discharge Position Explorer
description: The learner explores how rotation, discharge angle and viewpoint redraw an SWSI housing, then names the rotation and discharge position of ten drive-side and inlet-side drawings with hints and reasons as feedback.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Naming rotation and discharge position from the drive side
learningObjectives: The learner will apply the drive-side viewing rule and the discharge-angle convention to name the rotation and discharge position of ten SWSI centrifugal housing drawings, with at least 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: mirror image of an opposite-side view

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; option buttons use aria-pressed with a ✓ prefix; Enter checks and goes to the next drawing; the angle slider moves with the arrow keys.

equations: inlet-side view: d → 360 − d, arrow reversed
rules: An answer is correct only when rotation and abbreviation both match
Two attempts; only first-attempt answers count; mastery 8 of 10
limitations: Schematic housing drawings, not to scale

sources: FanPedia pp. 46–47 (SWSI Centrifugal Fans, Rotation View From Drive Side)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore the mapping first, then name ten judged drawings including mirrored inlet-side views
keyQuestions: What rotation and discharge does this fan have, seen from the drive side?
commonMisconceptions: The rotation seen from the inlet side is the fan's rotation
The discharge angle is a fixed compass bearing that ignores rotation
Upblast and downblast housings are the same for both rotations
"Top Horizontal" alone tells you which way the air goes
assessmentOpportunities: Running line 'Correct on first attempt: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
